name: Sable Freight Longhaul Flannel
description:
A heavyweight flannel shirt in a traditional two-color plaid — navy and grey, or rust and charcoal — with a full button front and a chest pocket on each side. The fabric is a brushed synthetic-wool that has nearly the same hand as real flannel but doesn't compress or mat with repeated washing. Reinforced at the collar, cuffs, and pocket corners. Cut generously through the chest and shoulders to allow layering over a thermal base. Long tails can be tucked or worn out.

Sable Freight issues these as optional cold-weather supplement to standard uniform sets, but they've migrated well beyond the logistics workforce. They're durable, warm, and cost less than most of their competitors. You'll find them on dock workers layered over Ironpass thermals, on Tier 2 families at weekend markets, on Shelf residents who acquired them secondhand, and on Tier 3 people who like the aesthetic and appreciate that the quality is real. The Sable Freight logo tag is small and easily removed.
what_it_says: You're practical. You've been outside. You're probably going to be outside again.
story_hooks: A Sable Freight flannel found at a crime scene has a Shelf-market vendor's repair stitching — which leads back to a specific stall that may have handled stolen cargo.
Sable Logistics is quietly phasing out the flannel from their uniform supplement program, and the workers who rely on it are organizing a response.
A character inherits one of these from someone who disappeared on a long-haul run — sewn inside the sleeve hem is a transit manifest for a cargo that officially doesn't exist.

physical_description.visual_profile: A substantial, workwear-inspired flannel shirt with a relaxed yet structured silhouette. The traditional two-color plaid pattern (navy/grey or rust/charcoal) reads as deliberately understated—functional rather than fashionable. Worn open over layers or buttoned, it projects honest utility and weathered authenticity.
physical_description.fit: Generously cut through chest and shoulders with enough room for thermal base layers underneath. Straight through the torso with long tails that hit mid-hip when untucked. Sleeves are full enough to accommodate augmentation interfaces or heavy gloves without binding. Deliberately non-tapered—built for work, not ego.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed synthetic-wool blend. Replicates traditional flannel hand-feel without compression fatigue. Maintains softness and loft through repeated washing cycles. Slightly heavier weight than casual flannels—substantial enough to hold structure even when layered.
physical_description.texture: Soft brushed nap on surface with a subtle grid weave underneath. Worn examples develop a faded, slightly fuzzy patina. Not slick or synthetic-feeling despite being lab-grown fibers. Collar and cuffs show subtle reinforcement stitching visible up close.
physical_description.color_scheme: Traditional two-tone plaid: either navy and grey (cooler, professional) or rust and charcoal (earthier, warmer). The pattern is classic, symmetrical, and reads instantly as 'working class authenticity.' Off-white button thread and minimal branding.
physical_description.closures: Full button front with standard resin buttons. Chest pockets have reinforced button closures. No zippers or snaps—pure analog fastening.
distinctive_features: Small Sable Freight logo tag (commonly removed by second and third-hand wearers)
Reinforced collar, cuffs, and pocket corners with visible topstitching
Dual chest pockets with button closures
Long tails designed for tucking or leaving out
Worn examples show faded plaid and softened edges
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 boundary. Tier 2 corp families and Tier 3 working class both claim ownership. Marketed as logistics uniform supplement but adopted across demographics because quality is genuinely good and pricing is fair.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals honest labor, reliability, and practical aesthetics. Worn by dock workers, Iowan Behemoth maintenance crews, cold-weather delivery personnel, and anyone who values durability over hype. The removed logo tag (or presence of it) indicates whether wearer is active logistics or scavenged/secondhand. Anti-fashion statement—very GLMZ.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and comfortable. Plaid fades slightly with washing. Collar edges soften. Active workers show grease stains, small tears patched or left raw. Secondhand versions may have faded unevenly or show ink marks from previous owners. Rarely pristine—the aesthetic demands lived-in authenticity.
